title: Propose with the Gradient, Accept with the Loss: One Hedged Attack for Pixel-Sparse Robustness
abstract: arXiv:2611.22596v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A pixel-sparse adversary may change a few pixels of an image to any value. Robustness to such attacks is currently measured with an ensemble, sparse-AutoAttack (sAA), because its members fail in different places: sparse projected gradient descent (sPGD) trusts a first-order model that a full pixel change breaks, and sparse random search (Sparse-RS) ignores the gradient even where it is informative. We show that both attacks are local searches, each a proposal distribution plus an acceptance rule, and ask what such a search can learn from the gradient. A Taylor bound says what to measure, and measurements at the states the search visits give five rules. The sign of the gradient is its most reliable use at a single pixel and sets a new pixel's value. Its ranking of candidate pixels should be followed loosely, and its ranking of the pixels to remove, which is often more reliable, can be followed more closely. A pixel should not be propose

translated_title: 用梯度提议，用损失接受：一种面向像素稀疏鲁棒性的对冲攻击
translated_abstract: 像素稀疏攻击者可以将图像中的少数几个像素更改为任意值。目前对这类攻击的鲁棒性是通过一个集成方法——稀疏AutoAttack（sAA）来衡量的，因为其各个成员会在不同的地方失败：稀疏投影梯度下降（sPGD）信任一阶模型，而完整的像素改变会破坏这一模型；稀疏随机搜索（Sparse-RS）即使在梯度信息可靠的地方也忽略梯度。我们证明这两种攻击本质上都是局部搜索，即一个提议分布加上一个接受规则，并探究这样的搜索能够从梯度中学到什么。泰勒界指出了应该测量什么，而在搜索所访问的状态处进行的测量得出了五条规则。梯度的符号是其在单个像素上最可靠的使用方式，可用来设定新像素的取值。梯度对候选像素的排名应当被宽松地遵循，而它对需要移除像素的排名（通常更为可靠）则可以被更严格地遵循。一个像素不应该被提议……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该论文将稀疏对抗攻击视为“提议分布加接受规则”的局部搜索，基于泰勒界推导出五条何时以及如何信任梯度符号、候选像素排名和移除像素排名的规则，提出了一种融合梯度与随机搜索优点的对冲式攻击，从而更准确地评估图像分类器的像素稀疏鲁棒性。
en_tdlr: This paper treats sparse adversarial attacks as local searches consisting of a proposal distribution and an acceptance rule, and derives five rules—based on a Taylor bound—on when and how to trust the gradient's sign, its ranking of candidate pixels, and its ranking of pixels to remove, yielding a hedged attack that combines the strengths of gradient-based and random-search methods for more accurate pixel-sparse robustness evaluation.
